name: capture_session_mutate
title: Change a footage session
description: One footage-session change per call: add_recordings, camera_group_set, listening_reference_set, remove_recording, set_recording_start, or retry_analysis. add_recordings attaches existing project recordings (top-level recording_ids) and schedules incremental chronology analysis (bytes still on a device, or a later upload from another camera operator, arrive through upload_link_create with capture_session_id); membership is retry-safe and never creates unrelated top-level episodes. camera_group_set assigns the top-level recording_ids to one stable camera group without changing chronology, source identity, or coverage: it never advances the chronology revision, never returns the session to analysis, and never queues another solve (without camera_group_key it mints a new group; camera_label renames without becoming identity; camera identity carries its own generation, and expected_camera_generation is required so a concurrent camera edit cannot be silently overwritten; the receipt retains prior keys and labels so grouping reverses through the same action). listening_reference_set chooses the default speech-rich listening reference camera via top-level recording_id, or omits it to restore automatic selection; it never selects Program camera or audio, discards transcripts, or overrides speaker identity. remove_recording is a revision-guarded, audited exclusion of one recording (top-level recording_id) that preserves the original recording, membership history, observations, and solve receipts. set_recording_start is an audited placement correction setting one unresolved recording's start on the stable capture clock; its reason records the capture evidence or human instruction behind the placement. retry_analysis retries the same evidence revision after bounded automatic chronology attempts have failed; it applies when next_action.kind is retry_analysis, with one idempotency key per exact terminal failure generation. Subject references ride top-level: capture_session_id always; recording_id / recording_ids per action.

recording_id.description: Recording public ID for listening_reference_set (optional; absent means automatic), remove_recording, and set_recording_start.

recording_ids.description: Recording public IDs for add_recordings and camera_group_set.

expected_revision.description: Current footage-session revision. Required for every action except add_recordings; a stale revision is rejected.

expected_camera_generation.description: Required for camera_group_set: the camera-identity generation this decision was made against, from manifest.camera_grouping.camera_generation. Camera identity has its own generation because grouping never advances the footage-session revision, so expected_revision cannot detect a concurrent camera decision. Omitting it is rejected; a stale one is rejected.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-stable key for safe retry of this exact change.

action.description: One footage-session action. Subject references (capture_session_id, recording_id, recording_ids) ride top-level.

relative_paths.description: Optional map from recording ID to a safe device/folder-relative path retained as ingest context.

camera_group_key.description: Optional existing group key from this session; a new group is created when omitted.

camera_label.description: Optional human label. Renaming never changes group identity.

reason.description: Required evidence or explicit human instruction supporting the grouping.
Optional concise reason retained with the preference receipt.
Optional concise reason retained in the audit receipt.

capture_start_seconds.description: Recording start on the session's stable capture clock. May be negative when footage predates the coordinate origin.

reason.description: Required concise rationale citing the capture evidence or explicit human instruction that establishes this placement.

dispatch_status.description: retry_analysis only: durable queue-delivery state for this retry receipt.

camera_generation.description: camera_group_set only: the footage session's camera-identity generation after this call, which the next camera edit takes as expected_camera_generation.
